previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for evaluation of an upper gastrointestinal bleed after reporting blood-tinged emesis and a drop in hematocrit from 43.5 to 32.7. Given his history of Hep C cirrhosis and esophageal varices, he was monitored closely with serial hematocrits, which stabilized and improved to 34.9, suggesting no ongoing active bleeding. He was continued on IV pantoprazole and observed without need for transfusion. He had significant fluid retention due to noncompliance with diuretics, having gained 25 pounds recently; after receiving IV furosemide and restarting spironolactone, he had good urine output and symptom improvement. An abdominal ultrasound revealed cirrhosis and an 8-mm indeterminate liver lesion, prompting a recommendation for MRI follow-up. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout and was discharged home with medication adjustments and instructions to resume all prescribed therapies, including diuretics, and to follow up in the liver clinic.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and Plan: ___ YO M w HCV cirrhosis presenting with 
BRBPR and confusion.  
.  
# BRBPR. The patient was guaiac negative, with a negative NG 
lavage, in the ED. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout 
the admission. His hematocrit stabilized then improved, without 
any transfusions. He received IV PPI on admission, but this was 
quickly changed to PO form, as there was low suspicion of 
ongoing GI bleed.
.  
# Confusion. The patient's presentation was attributed to 
hepatic encphalopathy, given his reported skipped doses of 
lactulose, as well as his rapid improvement once lactulose was 
restarted. As on his last admission, the importance of 
maintaining a regular dosing schedule for lactulose and 
rifaximin is crucial, to help avoid recurrent episodes of 
confusion or somnolence. Blood and urine cultures had no growth 
at time of discharge. He had no ascites on exam, so it was 
thought unlikely that his confusion could be secondary to SBP. 
Toxicology screens were negative.
.  
# HCV cirrhosis: c/b grade 2 gastric and esophageal varices, 
recurrent episodes of encephalopathy.  The patient was continued 
on lasix, spironolactone, nadolol, lactulose and rifaximin. The 
patient was discharged with close hepatology and psych follow-up 
scheduled.

Discharge Instructions:
Mr ___,

You were admitted to ___ for confusion and bloody stools. It 
was believed that your confusion was due to hepatic 
encephalopathy and you were started on your regular doses of 
lactulose and rifaximin. You had a CT scan of your head which 
did not show any acute intracranial abnormalities. Your mental 
status improved with the lactulose and rifaximin, back to your 
baseline levels. In regards to your potentially bloody stools, 
your stool was negative for containing blood in the ED. You 
underwent nasogastric lavage, which was also negative for blood. 
Your hematocrit levels were stable, and your blood pressure and 
heart rate remained stable as well.
.
It is very important for you to take your lactulose and 
rifaximin as prescribed by your providers, to avoid further 
episodes of hepatic encephalopathy. It is also very important 
for you to keep your appointments with the transplant clinic and 
your primary care physician (see below).
.
We made the following changes to your medications:
-Increased LACTULOSE to 60 mL, three times daily. Please take as 
much lactulose is necessary to have ___ bowel movements per day, 
as this will decreased your likelihood to have recurrent 
episodes of hepatic encephalopathy
-Added OMEPRAZOLE 20 mg, once daily

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHS:  Again noted are the bilateral hilar
calcified granulomas, unchanged.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette and
pulmonary vasculature are normal.  There is linear left lower lobe opacity,
compatible with left lower lobe subsegmental atelectasis.  The lungs are
otherwise clear without pleural effusion, pneumothorax or focal airspace
consolidations.  The osseous structures are grossly intact.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intrathoracic process.
2.  Unchanged bilateral hilar calcified granulomas.
